learningObjectives: Explain how containers package Python applications and dependencies.
Create the essential components of a Python Docker image.
Configure environment variables and application ports for containers.

activities.title: Container Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the components involved in running a Python application in a container.

content.concept: A container image packages application code and its runtime dependencies into a reproducible filesystem environment. A running container is an instance of that image.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides the starting filesystem and runtime environment, such as a Python base image.
Packages listed in requirements.txt or another dependency specification are installed into the image.
The Python source files and application assets are copied into the image.
Configuration values can be supplied to the running container without hard-coding them into the image.
The application listens on a port inside the container that can be mapped to a host or platform port.
Defines the command used to start the application when the container runs.

activities.title: Dockerfile Sequencer
activities.instruction: Arrange the major Dockerfile steps for a Python application.

content.concept: A Dockerfile commonly starts from a base image, establishes a working directory, installs dependencies, copies application code, and defines how the application starts.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Container Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble the essential parts of a Python Docker image.

content.concept: A useful Python image needs a suitable runtime, dependencies, application code, and a command that starts the service.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Container Configuration Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the configuration that correctly separates application settings from the image.

content.concept: Runtime configuration such as database URLs, API keys, and environment-specific settings should generally be supplied through environment variables or a secrets mechanism rather than hard-coded into the image.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Read DATABASE_URL from an environment variable
Hard-code a production database password in Dockerfile
Commit an API key directly into the image source
Store environment-specific secrets in application source code
config.answer: Read DATABASE_URL from an environment variable
